summary: Wrote src/en/module_03/30-exercises.md: the Exercises section ({#exercises}) with an introduction (grades one to three stars; 7 one-star = 35 min, 7 two-star = 70 min, 1 three-star = 25 min, 130 min in all; solutions hidden until opened) and all 15 exercises e1-e15 in plan order, each as ::: exercise followed by ::: solution. Every number was computed with labpy.sh. Solutions with code (e1, e2, e3 twice, e5, e6, e9, e10, e13, e14) include complete code that was run, with its real output pasted in. node tools/check.mjs --module 3 --lang en reports 0 errors (the 6 warnings concern other parts: undrawn figures, missing widgets, session anchors).
changes: e3: the plan says every unit of the last 7x7 map can see the whole image. Not quite. The theoretical field is 435 and units centre on input position 32*i, so the corner unit (i = 0) covers rows and columns 0-217 and never the last 6; the other units see all 224. Verified with a positive-weight, average-pool gradient-support run. Also added the closed form 14*Delta per stride-2 stage as a cross-check.

e7: the plan says 90-degree rotations confuse 6 and 9. It is a 180-degree rotation (or a vertical flip) that turns 6 into 9. The solution says so, and says a 90-degree rotation produces images no writer produces. The chest X-ray horizontal flip is marked 'doubtful', with the reason, not 'no'.

e14 (5): the plan's marching-cubes figures hold (887, +21% on the binary mask; 755, +3.4% blurred; scikit-image 0.26), but its explanation is incomplete. Measured: the +21% does not shrink with finer voxels of the same shape (+21.4%, +21.0%, +21.3% at 1x, 0.5x, 0.25x), and with isotropic 0.4 um voxels it is +8.9%. So the bias comes from the binary field together with the voxel aspect ratio, not from resolution. With a 0.5 um blur the area goes to -0.4% and -1.0% at the finer grids (the blur shrinks a convex body). The solution states this, and tabulates the volume sd per halving of the voxel size (35.0, 11.4, 2.6, 0.66, about 4x each) and the face-count bias converging to +46.2%.

e14: the exact area 730.6 and Thomsen 731.1 were confirmed (the elliptic-integral formula agrees with a brute-force surface integral to 6 digits). All other plan numbers reproduced: 7,005 voxels, 1,681.2 (+0.3%), 20 offsets mean 1,676.9 (+0.08%) and sd 11.4 (0.68%), faces 1,077.4 (+47.5%, limit 1,068.1), isotropic misread 448.3 (27%), boundary +0.25 um gives +11.0% (184 um^3).

e13: the prompt now says that level 0 is at full resolution (the plan was ambiguous). All numbers (648/162/40.5/10.1 MiB, 860.6 per patch, 3,442.5 MiB = 3.36 GiB, 7.22 GiB with decoder and weights, sides 80 -> 58% and 72 -> 42%, 108 vs 128 MiB) confirmed.

e9: uses its own numbers (19,990 background anchors at p_t = 0.98, 10 positives at p_t = 0.2: the negatives are 96.2% of the cross-entropy and 1.5% of the focal loss; an alpha weight of 10/19,990 shrinks a confident false positive's loss from 1.609 to 0.0008) so as not to repeat s11's worked example. RetinaNet's alpha = 0.25 on positives was kept.

e6: added to the plan's solution a numerical check that autograd's Jacobian equals the product of D_i(I + J_i) to 4e-16 and that a switched-off unit's diagonal entry falls from about 1 to 0. In (b) the solution points out that a plain gain of 0.98 gives exactly the same arithmetic as the residual -0.02 row, so the difference is where the number comes from, not the arithmetic. 0.95^100 = 0.0059, 1.05^100 = 131.5, 1.02^100 = 7.24, 0.98^100 = 0.133, alternating 0.980: all confirmed.

e10: IoUs 0.600/0.243/0.376, NMS results (A, C, D at 0.5 and 0.3; A, C at 0.2) and AP 1.000 with NMS and 0.833 without confirmed by code. e1, e2 and e5 (22.1x; 460,992 vs 21,120 parameters; 722.5 vs 32.7 MFLOPs; +8.0%) confirmed against PyTorch layers; the e1 solution adds the gcd(s, d) explanation of the unread rows and the 16-of-49 pixel count in 2D.

e4: the Lab 2 numbers in the prompt were reproduced by an independent re-run of the configuration (seeds 0-2, 40 epochs, Adam 3e-3): 0.931, 0.893, 0.440; parameter counts 6,218, 11,018, 6,151 confirmed. The solution adds the training accuracies from that re-run (flatten 1.00, GAP about 0.98) and labels them as a re-run, since Lab 2's own printout may differ in the last digit.
issues: 12-concepts-c.md, s13's worked example says marching cubes on the binary mask gives +21% 'because the 2 um slices leave terraces'. My runs for exercise e14 and for s13's own ellipsoid show that this holds only in the sense of voxel anisotropy: spacing 0.5x0.5x2.0 gives +21.6%, 0.5x0.5x1.0 +13.9%, isotropic 0.5 +8.8%, and 0.25x0.25x1.0 (same 4:1 shape, finer) +21.3%, so refinement alone does not remove it. Consider rewording to 'because the binary field puts every vertex at an edge midpoint and the voxels are anisotropic'. Exercise e14's solution (item 5) already says this.

scikit-image is not in the lab environment. To run e14 step 5 I installed scikit-image 0.26.0 and its small dependencies into a private directory under the session scratchpad (pip --target, used through PYTHONPATH) and did not touch the shared venv. The e14 code guards the import with try/except, so the exercise runs without it.

Exercises e4 and e8 rely on Lab 2 and Lab 4 behaviour (0.93/0.89/0.44 and the parameter counts; the first block transfers, the frozen probe is poor). Lab 2 is not in the part files that exist yet, so if its final printed accuracies differ materially from about 0.93 and 0.89, the prompt of e4 and the figures in its solution need a matching edit. e8 quotes no Lab 4 numbers.

Cross-references used by this part: Sections 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, Labs 2, 3, 4, 6, Module 01 Sections 8 and 10, all present as ids; the text of s3, s8, s12 and s13 was read, s11 and s14 were taken from the plan.
